definitions.rationale: This macro equation defines the named solutionModule proof term as the exact MPY constructor representation of the Python implementation.
definitions.text:
rule solutionModule
    => Module(
         FuncDef("largest_prime_factor", Params("n"),
           Assign(Name("factor"), Int(2))
           While(Compare(Name("n"), CmpOp(">", Name("factor"))),
             If(Compare(
               BinOp("%", Name("n"), Name("factor")),
               CmpOp("==", Int(0))),
               Assign(Name("n"),
                 BinOp("//", Name("n"), Name("factor"))),
               AugAssign(Name("factor"), "+", Int(1))))
           Return(Name("factor"))))

definitions.rationale: This macro equation defines the named lpfCondition proof fragment used by the loop claim.
This macro equation defines the named lpfStep proof fragment used by the loop claim.
definitions.text:
rule lpfStep
    => If(Compare(
         BinOp("%", Name("n"), Name("factor")),
         CmpOp("==", Int(0))),
         Assign(Name("n"), BinOp("//", Name("n"), Name("factor"))),
         AugAssign(Name("factor"), "+", Int(1)))

definitions.rationale: This is the base equation of the lpfSpec mathematical recurrence, returning the current factor when the residual is no larger.
definitions.text:
rule lpfSpec(N:Int, F:Int) => F
    requires N <=Int F

definitions.rationale: This equation defines the divisible branch of the lpfSpec recurrence by removing one occurrence of the current factor.
definitions.text:
rule lpfSpec(N:Int, F:Int)
    => lpfSpec((N -Int pyMod(N, F)) /Int F, F)
    requires N >Int F andBool pyMod(N, F) ==Int 0

definitions.rationale: This equation defines the nondivisible branch of the lpfSpec recurrence by advancing to the next candidate factor.
definitions.text:
rule lpfSpec(N:Int, F:Int) => lpfSpec(N, F +Int 1)
    requires N >Int F andBool pyMod(N, F) =/=Int 0

operational_rules.rationale: This priority-40 observation rule executes the program's symbolic loop comparison by reading n and factor from the active scope; it is part of the verification execution model and was not separately proved.
operational_rules.text:
rule <k>
         Compare(Name("n"), CmpOp(">", Name("factor")))
         => N >Int F
         ...
       </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes>
         ... L |-> scope(
           ("n" |-> N:Int) ("factor" |-> F:Int) _REST:Map,
           _P:Parent)
         ...
       </scopes>
       [priority(40)]

operational_rules.rationale: This priority-40 observation rule executes the program's symbolic remainder-equality test from the active scope; it is an operational accelerator present during the proof, not a separately established lemma.
operational_rules.text:
rule <k>
         Compare(
           BinOp("%", Name("n"), Name("factor")),
           CmpOp("==", Int(0)))
         => pyMod(N, F) ==Int 0
         ...
       </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes>
         ... L |-> scope(
           ("n" |-> N:Int) ("factor" |-> F:Int) _REST:Map,
           _P:Parent)
         ...
       </scopes>
       [priority(40)]

operational_rules.rationale: This priority-40 state-transition rule executes the exact floor-division assignment to n and updates the current scope, making it an operational rule of the verification model.
operational_rules.text:
rule <k>
         Assign(Name("n"), BinOp("//", Name("n"), Name("factor")))
         => .K
         ...
       </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes>
         ... L |-> scope(
           ("n" |-> N:Int) ("factor" |-> F:Int) REST:Map
           => ("n" |-> ((N -Int pyMod(N, F)) /Int F))
              ("factor" |-> F) REST,
           _P:Parent)
         ...
       </scopes>
       [priority(40)]

operational_rules.rationale: This priority-40 state-transition rule executes the exact augmented assignment that increments factor, so it belongs to the verification model's operational behavior.
operational_rules.text:
rule <k>
         AugAssign(Name("factor"), "+", Int(1))
         => .K
         ...
       </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes>
         ... L |-> scope(
           ("n" |-> N:Int) ("factor" |-> F:Int) REST:Map
           => ("n" |-> N) ("factor" |-> (F +Int 1)) REST,
           _P:Parent)
         ...
       </scopes>
       [priority(40)]

operational_rules.rationale: This priority-40 control rule executes return of factor by setting the return state and continuing with #pop; it is an ordinary operational shortcut included in the proof model.
operational_rules.text:
rule <k> Return(Name("factor")) ~> _ => #pop </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes>
         ... L |-> scope(
           ("factor" |-> F:Int) _REST:Map,
           _P:Parent)
         ...
       </scopes>
       <ret> noRet => retV(F) </ret>
       [priority(40)]

source_rules.rationale: This simplification asserts a freshness-conditioned equality for deletion by Map update over an existing Map operator. It defines no new summary or named proof term, and Stage 1 compiles it into VERIFICATION before the only kprove invocation, so it is an additional unproved mathematical fact rather than a proved derived lemma.
source_rules.text:
rule ((L:Int |-> _V:Scope) M:Map) [ L <- undef ] => M
    requires notBool (L in_keys(M))
    [simplification]
